scenes.title: Find the claims underneath the idea
scenes.visual: Founder reviews an anonymous validation brief.
scenes.narration: Every opportunity depends on claims that could be wrong. An assumption register makes those claims visible. Start with your specific group, task and proposed benefit. Listing assumptions is not evidence that they are true, and this lesson does not automatically choose what to test first.

scenes.title: Separate different kinds of claims
scenes.visual: Editable problem, benefit, behaviour, buyer and delivery cards.
scenes.narration: People experience a difficulty, people value an improvement, people change behaviour, someone approves or pays, and we can deliver the approach are different claims. Evidence for one does not prove the others. Keep user and possible buyer roles separate.

scenes.title: Write a claim that could be wrong
scenes.visual: Editable specific group and context statement.
scenes.narration: Write each assumption as one specific claim, with a group and context. Avoid vague statements such as everyone loves convenience. If the buyer or payment terms are unknown, say so. Do not invent prices, customer quotes or commitments to complete a register.

scenes.title: Record evidence and consequences
scenes.visual: Editable claim, status, source and consequence columns.
scenes.narration: For each claim, record the evidence basis, what remains unknown and what would happen if it were false. Plans remain plans. A provider’s description, a compliment or a single account has limits. Note dependencies: if permission is unavailable, a planned observation cannot proceed.

scenes.title: Identify candidate risk without false precision
scenes.visual: Editable uncertainty and consequence cards without totals.
scenes.narration: An assumption may be risky when it is uncertain and its failure would materially change the opportunity or block the next step. Explain your judgment; do not add guessed numbers into a success score. Several claims can remain unresolved. Prioritising the next test comes in Lesson 23.

scenes.title: Build the assumption register
scenes.narration: Create your Assumption Register with problem, benefit, behaviour, buyer and delivery claims. Preserve sources and unknowns, identify a candidate risk and a disconfirming signal, then plan a small ethical check. This is a learning register, not validated demand or permission to run a test.

children: An
assumption
is a claim that could be wrong.
Risk
concerns uncertainty and the consequence if it is wrong. A
dependency
is something another step relies on, such as access permission.
Problem
The difficulty occurs and matters for this group/context.
Benefit
The proposed improvement matters enough to investigate.
Behaviour
People might use or switch to the approach despite effort and habits.
Buyer / payment
A particular role may approve or pay under defined conditions. Unknown roles or terms stay unknown.
Access / delivery
You can obtain permission, perform the check and potentially deliver the approach. A named contact is not confirmed access.
Illustrative example:
a visitor asks staff for directions. That may support an observed interaction, not importance, switching, payment or your ability to deliver a service. Record each claim separately.
Write a specific claim for each category.
Record source/status and what remains unknown.
Explain what changes if the claim is wrong.
Note dependencies and a disconfirming signal.
Name a candidate high-risk assumption with reasons.
No automatic scores or ranking are calculated. Lesson 23 will prioritise what to test first. Unknown is acceptable with a check; do not invent a price, quote or commitment.
Review validation starting brief
